milestones.label: Regularity structures introduced
milestones.work: M. Hairer, A theory of regularity structures, arXiv:1303.5113 (2013)
milestones.description: The public preprint introduces regularity structures as a framework for singular stochastic PDEs.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the preprint to March 2013 and describes the new structure.

milestones.label: Phi-four-three dynamics constructed
milestones.work: M. Hairer, A theory of regularity structures, arXiv:1303.5113 (2013)
milestones.description: The same preprint applies the framework to construct a Markov process associated with the Phi-four-three model.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly names the Phi-four-three application.

milestones.note: The same paper truly plays both the first-statement and first-application roles.

notes: The public 2013 preprint predates the 2014 Inventiones issue. Earlier rough-path and renormalization work is contextual, not itself a regularity structure; institutional naming remains open.

canonicalName: Entropy proves the polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture

milestones.label: Entropy proof of PFR posted
milestones.work: W. T. Gowers, B. Green, F. Manners and T. Tao, On a conjecture of Marton, arXiv:2311.05762 (2023)
milestones.description: The public preprint proves the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture in characteristic two by an entropy-based argument.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the proof to November 2023 and states the characteristic-two result.
Coauthor Tao describes the entropy argument used in the new proof.

notes: This event denotes the 2023 proof, not the original conjecture. The arXiv abstract says odd-characteristic details were to follow; no earlier publication year is inferred from conjecture history. Institutional date remains open.

milestones.label: Rough-signal differential equation theory begins
milestones.work: T. Lyons, Differential equations driven by rough signals (I): an extension of an inequality of L. C. Young, Math. Res. Lett. 1 (1994)
milestones.description: The 1994 paper publicly develops an approach to differential equations driven by rough signals.

evidence.claim: Oxford’s bibliographic record identifies the 1994 paper.

milestones.label: Systematic rough-path treatment
milestones.work: T. Lyons, Differential equations driven by rough signals, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 14 (1998)
milestones.description: A long paper systematically treats differential equations under rough driving signals.

evidence.claim: EMS journal record identifies the 1998 treatment.

works.citation: Differential equations driven by rough signals (I): an extension of an inequality of L. C. Young
works.whyItMatters: Started the rough-signal differential equation theory

notes: The inherited 1998 citation is a consolidation, not the earliest public paper. First external target application and named institution remain open.

milestones.label: Fourier method applied to four-term progressions
milestones.work: W. T. Gowers, A new proof of Szemerédi’s theorem for arithmetic progressions of length four, GAFA 8 (1998)
milestones.description: Gowers developed quantitative uniformity methods for four-term arithmetic progressions.

evidence.claim: The 1998 journal record identifies the four-term proof.

milestones.label: Higher-order uniformity method extended
milestones.work: W. T. Gowers, A new proof of Szemerédi’s theorem, GAFA 11 (2001)
milestones.description: The longer proof develops uniformity methods across progression lengths.

works.citation: A new proof of Szemerédi’s theorem

notes: The phrase higher-order Fourier analysis became standard later. Earliest public statement under that formulation, first use on a distinct target problem and institutional naming remain open.

milestones.label: Finite-field sum–product estimate
milestones.work: J. Bourgain, N. Katz and T. Tao, A sum-product estimate in finite fields, and applications, GAFA 14 (2004)
milestones.description: The paper develops a major additive–multiplicative tool with applications.

evidence.claim: Publisher record dates the paper to 2004.

milestones.label: Additive Combinatorics monograph
milestones.work: T. Tao and V. H. Vu, Additive Combinatorics, Cambridge University Press (print 2006)
milestones.description: A named textbook organizes the field under additive combinatorics.

evidence.claim: Cambridge lists the print publication as September 2006; electronic publication is later.

notes: The 2006 print book is a reproducible institutional anchor; Cambridge’s digital edition is dated 2010 and must not replace the print year. The first public statement of additive combinatorics as a field and first title use still need a database-wide search.

milestones.label: Jones-polynomial categorification posted
milestones.work: M. Khovanov, A categorification of the Jones polynomial, arXiv:math/9908171 (1999)
milestones.description: The public preprint constructs a bigraded link cohomology whose Euler characteristic is the Jones polynomial.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the public manuscript to August 1999 and states the construction.

works.citation: A categorification of the Jones polynomial

notes: The 2000 Duke journal issue follows the 1999 public preprint. The first separate application and named institution remain open.

canonicalName: Random matrix universality and Dyson / Tracy-Widom in KPZ

milestones.label: Growth fluctuations linked to Tracy–Widom law
milestones.work: K. Johansson, Shape Fluctuations and Random Matrices, arXiv:math/9903134 (1999)
milestones.description: Johansson’s public paper shows a growth-model fluctuation law converging to the GUE Tracy–Widom distribution.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the preprint to March 1999 and states the Tracy–Widom limit.

notes: The inherited Okounkov random-partitions citation does not by itself establish the KPZ–Tracy–Widom bridge; Johansson’s direct paper is used. Broader universality and first application dates remain open.

milestones.label: Lattice paths count curves in toric surfaces
milestones.work: G. Mikhalkin, Counting curves via lattice paths in polygons, arXiv:math/0209253 (2002)
milestones.description: The public note applies the emerging tropical viewpoint to enumerative curve counts.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the note to September 2002 and states its curve-counting application.

milestones.label: Enumerative tropical geometry elaborated
milestones.work: G. Mikhalkin, Enumerative tropical algebraic geometry in R2, arXiv:math/0312530 (2003)
milestones.description: The later preprint proves curve-enumeration formulas using tropical geometry.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the paper to December 2003 and references its 2002 announcement.

works.citation: Counting curves via lattice paths in polygons
works.whyItMatters: Applied tropical methods to curve counting

notes: The 2002 announcement predates the 2005 JAMS issue. The conceptual start of tropical geometry is earlier and needs separate priority research; the first named textbook is not yet adjudicated.

milestones.label: Holomorphic Casson invariant preprint
milestones.work: R. P. Thomas, A holomorphic Casson invariant for Calabi–Yau 3-folds, and bundles on K3 fibrations, arXiv:math/9806111 (1998)
milestones.description: Thomas’s public preprint defines a deformation-invariant holomorphic Casson invariant on Calabi–Yau threefolds.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the preprint to June 1998 and describes the invariant.

milestones.label: Motivic DT wall-crossing formalism
milestones.work: M. Kontsevich and Y. Soibelman, Stability structures, motivic Donaldson–Thomas invariants and cluster transformations, arXiv:0811.2435 (2008)
milestones.description: The preprint develops motivic DT invariants and wall-crossing formulas.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the public paper to November 2008 and states the wall-crossing results.

works.citation: A holomorphic Casson invariant for Calabi–Yau 3-folds, and bundles on K3 fibrations

notes: The 2000 journal issue follows Thomas’s 1998 public preprint. Earlier uses of the Donaldson–Thomas name, first target application of wall crossing and institutional recognition need research.

canonicalName: Random planar maps and the Brownian map

milestones.label: Brownian map named as quadrangulation limit
milestones.work: J.-F. Marckert and A. Mokkadem, Limit of normalized quadrangulations: The Brownian map, arXiv:math/0403398 (2004)
milestones.description: The public preprint names a random scaling-limit object the Brownian map.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the preprint to 2004 and the abstract explicitly names the Brownian map.

milestones.label: Universality proved for planar maps
milestones.work: J.-F. Le Gall, Uniqueness and universality of the Brownian map, arXiv:1105.4842 (2011)
milestones.description: The public paper proves convergence of multiple random-map families to a universal Brownian-map limit.

evidence.claim: ArXiv dates the preprint to 2011 and states the universality theorem.

works.citation: Uniqueness and universality of the Brownian map
works.whyItMatters: Proved universality for random planar maps

notes: The 2004 public introduction predates the 2013 published universality article. First application beyond quadrangulations and institutional recognition remain open.
